title_en: Regulations on the Administration of the Prevention and Control of Pollution Damage to the Marine Environment by Coastal Engineering Construction Projects of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Marine Environment Protection Law of the People's Republic of China for the purposes of strengthening the environmental protection management of coastal engineering construction projects, strictly controlling new pollution, and protecting and improving the marine environment.

Article 3 These Regulations shall apply to all entities and individuals that construct coastal engineering construction projects within the territory of the People's Republic of China.
The environmental protection management of ship-breaking yard construction projects shall be implemented in accordance with the Regulations on the Prevention of Environmental Pollution from Ship-Breaking.

Article 4 The construction of coastal engineering construction projects shall conform to the requirements of the regional environmental protection plan for the economic zone in which they are located.

Article 5 The competent department of environmental protection under the State Council shall be in charge of the environmental protection work for coastal engineering construction projects nationwide.
The competent departments of environmental protection of the local people's governments at or above the county level along the coast shall be in charge of the environmental protection work for coastal engineering construction projects within their respective administrative regions.

Article 6 The construction, renovation, and expansion of coastal engineering construction projects shall comply with the relevant provisions of the State on the environmental protection management of construction projects.

Article 7 The construction unit of a coastal engineering construction project shall, according to law, prepare an environmental impact report (form) and submit it to the competent department of environmental protection for approval.
Before approving the environmental impact report (form) of a coastal engineering construction project, the competent department of environmental protection shall solicit opinions from the departments in charge of marine affairs, maritime affairs, fisheries, and the environmental protection department of the military.
It is prohibited to reclaim land from the sea by enclosing areas that have navigable value in natural harbors, important seedling bases and breeding grounds, and the natural spawning grounds, breeding grounds, feeding grounds, and important migration channels of fish, shrimp, crab, shellfish, and algae on water surfaces and tidal flats.

Article 9 It is prohibited to construct Sino-foreign equity joint ventures, Sino-foreign contractual joint ventures, and wholly foreign-owned enterprises that transfer pollution to the sea areas and coasts of the People's Republic of China. Technologies and equipment introduced for coastal engineering construction projects shall have corresponding pollution prevention and control measures to prevent the transfer of pollution.

Article 10 In marine special protection areas, marine nature reserves, coastal scenic areas, salt field protection areas, seawater bathing beaches, important fishing waters, and other areas requiring special protection, no coastal engineering construction projects that pollute the environment or damage the landscape shall be constructed. Where coastal engineering construction projects are constructed outside such areas, they shall not damage the environmental quality of the aforementioned areas, unless otherwise provided by laws and regulations.

Article 11 When a coastal engineering construction project undergoes completion acceptance, the construction project may be formally put into production or use only after its environmental protection facilities have passed the acceptance inspection.

Article 12 The environmental protection authority under the people's government at or above the county level may, according to the project management authority, conduct on-site inspections of coastal engineering construction projects jointly with the relevant departments. The inspected party shall truthfully report the situation and provide information. The inspectors have the obligation to keep confidential the technical secrets and business secrets of the inspected party, except as otherwise provided by laws and regulations.

Article 13 Where facilities for discharging wastewater into the sea are installed, the self-purification capacity of seawater shall be reasonably utilized, and the location of the discharge outlet shall be carefully selected. Where underground ditches or pipelines are used for discharge, the outlet position of the water discharge pipe shall be below the low-tide line.

Article 14 When constructing a port or wharf, anti-pollution facilities commensurate with its throughput capacity and types of cargo shall be installed.
Ports, oil terminals, and chemical dangerous goods terminals shall be equipped with emergency equipment and apparatus for major marine pollution damage accidents.
Where an existing port or wharf fails to meet the requirements of the preceding two paragraphs, the environmental protection authority, jointly with the competent authority for ports and wharves, shall order it to install or equip such facilities within a specified time limit.

Article 15 When constructing a coastal shipyard or ship repair yard, reception and treatment facilities for residual oil and waste oil, reception and treatment facilities for oily wastewater, facilities for oil containment, oil recovery and oil dispersing, reception and treatment facilities for industrial wastewater, and reception and treatment facilities for industrial and ship garbage, among others, shall be installed commensurate with its nature and scale.

Article 16 When constructing a coastal nuclear power plant or other nuclear facilities, the relevant national provisions and standards on nuclear environmental protection and radiation protection shall be strictly observed.

Article 17 When constructing a coastal oil depot, reception and treatment facilities for oily wastewater, collection and treatment facilities for ground washing wastewater from the depot yard, and emergency facilities for accidents shall be installed; oil pipelines and oil storage facilities shall conform to the national provisions on leakage prevention and corrosion prevention.

Article 18 When constructing a coastal mine, during the processes of mining, mineral processing, transportation, storage, smelting and tailings treatment, measures to prevent pollution damage to the marine environment shall be taken in accordance with the relevant provisions.

Article 19 When constructing a coastal landfill site for garbage or industrial waste residue, protective dikes and a bottom sealing layer shall be built, and a system for collecting, discharging and treating leachate, as well as explosion-proof devices for flammable gases, shall be installed.

Article 20 When constructing coastal protection projects, or building water conservancy facilities, navigation channels or comprehensive regulation projects at the mouth of a river entering the sea, measures shall be taken so as not to damage the ecological environment and aquatic resources.

Article 21 When constructing coastal engineering projects, the living environment of wild animals and plants under key national or local protection shall not be altered or destroyed. No coastal engineering project that may cause pollution or destruction of the living environment of wild animals and plants under key protection shall be constructed; if such construction is truly necessary, consent shall be obtained from the competent administrative department for wild animals and plants, and the construction entity shall be responsible for organizing measures such as ex-situ breeding to ensure species continuity.
Where the construction of sluices or dams in the migration passages of fish, shrimp, crabs, or shellfish has a serious impact on fishery resources, the construction entity shall build fish passage facilities or take other remedial measures.

Article 22 Where a collective-owned entity or an individual constructs an aquaculture project that does not constitute a capital construction project in waters or tidal flats owned by the whole people, such construction shall be carried out within the areas planned by the local people's government at or above the county level.
Where a collective-owned entity or an individual engages in sporadic commercial extraction of sand and gravel, such extraction shall be carried out within the areas designated by the local people's government at or above the county level.
Article 23 It is prohibited to construct coastal engineering projects that destroy the ecosystems of mangroves and coral reefs in areas where mangroves and coral reefs grow.

Article 24 The construction of coastal engineering projects shall prevent abnormal coastal erosion.
It is prohibited to engage in activities such as blasting, extraction of sand and gravel, and soil removal that endanger the safety of coastal protection facilities within the protection zones of such facilities as prescribed by the administrative department for coastal protection facilities. Without approval from the relevant competent department authorized by the State Council, no coastal protection facility shall be occupied or dismantled.

Article 25 Where a coastal engineering project is constructed without a reviewed and approved environmental impact statement (form), penalties shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of Article 79 of the Marine Environment Protection Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 26 Where a party refuses or obstructs an on-site inspection by the competent department of environmental protection, or practices fraud during the inspection, the competent department of environmental protection of the people's government at or above the county level shall impose penalties in accordance with the provisions of Article 75 of the Marine Environment Protection Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 27 Where a coastal engineering project is put into production or use without the environmental protection facilities having been completed or meeting the prescribed requirements, penalties shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of Article 80 of the Marine Environment Protection Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 28 Where a staff member of the competent department of environmental protection abuses authority, neglects duties, or engages in graft, the entity to which he belongs or the competent authority at a higher level shall impose administrative sanctions; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with law.
Article 29 These Regulations shall come into force as of August 1, 1990.
